# URBAN IMPACTS GENERATED BY SITM: A COMPARIOUS LOOK AT THE CASES OF BOGOTA AND MEDELLIN (COLOMBIA)

This paper presents some results of a research in development on an Ex Post Economic Assessment of Integrated Mass Transport Systems (SITM) of the cities of Bogotá and Medellín respectively. The SITM of Bogotá (Transmilenio) is based on BRT (Bus Rapid Transit) buses, while the SITM of Medellín (Metro) is based on urban trains, two different technologies implanted as a backbone component of these systems. The estimation and comparative analysis of urban impacts is carried out, in terms of soil prices, derived from the implementation of SITM stations and road infrastructure for both cities. The model of differences in differences (DID) is used to estimate urban impacts, where the unit of study are the urban areas, the condition with treatment is given by the Direct Influence Area (ADI) of the SITM and the temporary condition is given by the evolution of SITM in annual periods. Considering the statistically significant impacts, it is identified that in the city of Bogotá the urban impacts generated by SITM have been negative while in the city of Medellín the impact has been positive
